D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Both plans cover the core ML/AI technical stack adequately. Plan 1 provides broader technical coverage including CNNs, NLP with Transformers, MLOps, and a specialization menu, resulting in 5 projects across diverse domains. Plan 2 focuses more deeply on a single capstone project built end-to-end with cloud deployment (AWS), MLOps tooling (MLFlow/DVC), and CI/CD integration, plus a second project in Month 3. Plan 2 integrates interview prep (LeetCode, ML system design, behavioral STAR) consistently across all three months, whereas Plan 1 concentrates interview prep heavily in Month 3. Plan 2's portfolio strategy is stronger for AI Engineering roles because it emphasizes deployed, production-ready systems with cloud endpoints — a key differentiator for global remote hiring. Plan 1's portfolio is broader but less deployment-focused until Month 3. Plan 2's explicit AWS deployment and MLOps integration make the final portfolio more employer-worthy for ML Engineer roles specifically.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 2 produces a cloud-deployed, MLOps-integrated capstone with CI/CD and consistent interview prep across all months, which is more directly aligned with what global ML Engineer employers evaluate.

D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility
D2.comparative_analysis: Plan 2 explicitly calculates total available hours (360 hours at 5h/day for ~72 days, though 3 months at 5h/day is closer to 450h — the 360h figure assumes ~72 working days which is reasonable with weekends), allocates 324 planned hours with 36 buffer hours, and breaks down theory/practice/project time per month. This transparency is a significant advantage. Plan 1 does not provide explicit hour budgets but describes a daily allocation breakdown (1.5-2h theory, 2-2.5h coding, 0.5-1h review). Plan 1's Week 3-4 of Month 2 is cognitively dense — covering advanced NLP preprocessing, embeddings, RNNs, Transformers, Hugging Face, AND model interpretability in two weeks is ambitious. Plan 2's cognitive load is better managed by focusing on one capstone project iteratively rather than switching between multiple distinct projects. Both plans have some overengineering risk: Plan 1 includes RL concepts and GANs as options; Plan 2 includes IaC/Terraform concepts. Plan 2's explicit buffer and hour accounting gives it a feasibility edge.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 2's explicit hour budgeting with buffer allocation and iterative single-capstone approach reduces cognitive overload compared to Plan 1's dense multi-topic weeks.
